name: Ugandan Matoke
description: Matoke, steamed and mashed green cooking bananas, is widely considered Uganda's national dish - real matoke bananas are a specific starchy variety, and green plantain is a much closer match than sweet yellow bananas, though still not identical.
steps_detailed: Steam the green plantain over simmering water 30-35 minutes until completely soft.
Mash roughly, then stir through the tomatoes and onion, simmered separately for 5 minutes and folded in.

name: Ugandan Luwombo
description: Luwombo, meat steamed inside a wrapped banana leaf parcel, is a genuine Buganda specialty traditionally reserved for special occasions - the wrapping seals in real steam and aroma that open cooking can't replicate.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot.
Wrap tightly in foil (standing in for banana leaf) and steam over simmering water 30-35 minutes to seal in the aroma.

name: Ugandan Groundnut Stew
description: A rich stew built on real ground peanuts, a beloved Ugandan dish shared in spirit with groundnut stews found across the wider region.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot.
Simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Ugandan Rolex
description: Rolex, a rolled chapati wrapped around an omelet, is one of Uganda's most beloved street foods, its name a playful shortening of 'rolled eggs'.
steps_detailed: Make a simple chapati from the flour, water, and a little oil, cooking in a hot, dry pan 2-3 minutes per side.
Whisk the eggs with the tomatoes and cabbage, and cook into a thin omelet.
Roll the omelet inside the warm chapati.

name: Ugandan Posho
description: Posho, a stiff maize porridge, is Uganda's most essential staple starch, closely related to Kenyan ugali and eaten daily alongside stews.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, 12-15 minutes until very thick and smooth.

name: Ugandan Chapati
description: Chapati, a soft, layered flatbread, reflects genuine Indian culinary influence and is one of Uganda's most beloved breads.
steps_detailed: Work the flour with warm water and half the oil into a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll thin, brush with the remaining oil, and coil before flattening again to build real layers.
Cook in a hot, dry pan, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden.

name: Ugandan Katogo
description: Katogo, matoke or cassava cooked together with beans or meat into one pot, a beloved Ugandan breakfast and everyday staple.

name: Ugandan Sukuma Wiki
description: Sukuma wiki, collard greens or kale simmered with onion and tomato, shared across much of East Africa including Uganda.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 5-6 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Add the kale and simmer 10-12 minutes until tender.

description: Nyama choma, grilled meat, is beloved across Uganda the same way it is throughout East Africa.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and lemon juice.
Grill, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

description: Mandazi, lightly sweet fried dough, a beloved Ugandan breakfast snack shared across East Africa.

Roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.
